features.title: Everything annoying, gone.
features.lead: AdRaze does more than hide banners. It stops the stuff that makes the web slow, irritating and sometimes dangerous.
features.ads_text: Banners, video ads and sponsored boxes never load. Empty ad slots are cleaned up so the page looks normal.
features.trackers_text: Analytics scripts and ad networks that follow you from site to site are blocked with EasyPrivacy.
features.popups_text: Ad windows that open wherever you click get stopped. Signing in with Google, Apple and BankID works as usual.
features.redirects_text: If an ad tries to send you to a scam site, you land on AdRaze's stop page instead. You decide whether to continue.
features.local_text: Frellwit's Swedish filter list takes care of the ads on Aftonbladet, Expressen, Blocket and the rest of the Swedish web.
features.pause_text: Want to support a site you like? One click in the menu pauses AdRaze just there.
photo.alt: A person relaxing on the sofa with a laptop on their lap
photo.title: The internet, without the nagging.
photo.text: No countdowns, no flashing banners, no windows popping up. Just what you came to read, watch or play.
steps.title: Up and running in ten seconds.
steps.s1_text: Click "Add to Chrome". No account, no sign-up.
steps.s2_text: AdRaze works in the background. The orange number on the icon shows how much it has blocked.
steps.s3_text: The filter lists get updated with new versions, so your protection keeps up as ads change.
open.title: Built in Sweden. Open to everyone.
open.text: AdRaze is open source under GPL-3. Anyone can read the code and see exactly what it does. It sends nothing to any server, not even ours.

faq.title: Questions and answers
faq.a1: No. AdRaze is free, with no hidden subscriptions, no "premium" and no ads of its own.
faq.q2: Do you collect data about me?
faq.a2: No. All filtering happens locally in your browser. The counter in the menu is only stored on your own computer.
faq.q3: Does it work in Brave, Edge and Opera?
faq.a3: Yes, AdRaze works in every Chromium-based browser. In Brave you can turn off Shields if you want AdRaze to do all the blocking.
faq.q4: A site tells me to turn off my ad blocker. What do I do?
faq.a4: Open the AdRaze menu and hit the button to pause on that site. Let us know which site it was and we'll try to fix it in the next version.
faq.q5: Can I still sign in with Google or pay with Klarna?
faq.a5: Yes. AdRaze always lets sign-ins and payments through when you click them yourself, like Google, Apple, Microsoft, PayPal, Klarna, Swish and BankID.
faq.a6: To "raze" something means to level it to the ground. That's exactly what it does to ads.

privacy.meta_description: Without an account, AdRaze collects no data. How the extension, the account and the permissions work.
privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.p_short: Without an account, AdRaze doesn't collect, store or send any information about you or what you do online. Everything happens locally in your browser. If you create an account, which is optional, we only store your email address and how many things were stopped per day. Never which sites you visit.
privacy.local1: The list of sites where you've paused AdRaze.
privacy.local2: Counters for how many pop-ups and redirects were stopped.
privacy.local4: Sites where you want to see the cookie banner yourself, and how many cookie banners were rejected.
privacy.p_local: This is saved using the browser's own storage (chrome.storage) and never leaves your computer. If you uninstall AdRaze, it's gone.
privacy.perm_dnr: declarativeNetRequest: blocks ads and trackers using Chrome's built-in filtering.
privacy.perm_hosts: Access to all websites: needed to hide empty ad slots and stop popups on the pages you visit. Page content is not read and is never sent anywhere.
privacy.perm_nav: webNavigation: to recognize popup windows opened by a page and close them if they lead to ads or dangerous sites.
privacy.perm_scripting: scripting: inserts style rules that hide ads and shows stats for the tab you have open.
privacy.perm_storage: storage: saves your paused sites and counters locally.
privacy.p_lists: AdRaze ships with filter lists from EasyList, EasyPrivacy, Frellwit's Swedish Filter, uBlock Origin, AdGuard and Peter Lowe. The lists are bundled with the extension. No requests about which pages you visit are sent to anyone.
privacy.p_third: AdRaze never sells data and doesn't share it with anyone. If you have an account, emails are sent through Brevo, and if you choose Google sign-in, Google confirms who you are. Nothing else leaves our server.
privacy.p_open: AdRaze is open source under GPL-3.0, so anyone can check exactly what the extension does.
privacy.p_changes: If this policy changes, the date at the top of this page will be updated.

privacy.p_account: You don't need an account to use AdRaze. It only exists so you can see your stats on adraze.app, from all your computers. This is then stored on our server:
privacy.acc_email: Email address, so you can sign in and receive verification codes.
privacy.acc_password: Password, stored only as a salted scrypt hash. We can never see your password.
privacy.acc_google: Google sign-in, if you choose it: we receive your email address and an ID number from Google, nothing else is stored.
privacy.acc_stats: Stats per day: the number of stopped ads, trackers, dangerous pages, pop-ups and redirects. Only numbers, never addresses, sites or searches.
privacy.acc_devices: Connected browsers: a name like "Chrome on Windows" and when it last sent stats.
privacy.acc_cookies: Two cookies on adraze.app: one that keeps you signed in and one that remembers the browser is already verified. No tracking cookies.
privacy.p_account_mail: Emails with verification codes are sent through Brevo. The server is in Sweden and is reached through Cloudflare. We use no analytics or ads on the account.
privacy.p_account_delete: You can delete your account at any time under Account on adraze.app. Your email address, stats and all connected browsers are then deleted immediately.
privacy.perm_feedback: declarativeNetRequestFeedback: counts how many ads, trackers and dangerous pages were stopped. The extension only reads which kind of rule matched, not which page it was on.
privacy.perm_alarms: alarms: updates the counters at regular intervals and sends the stats to your account if you have connected one.

kolla.lead: Paste a link. We check it against 11 security lists and open it in a real browser, first without and then with AdRaze.
kolla.label: Link to check
kolla.step_queue: In queue, position {n}. About half a minute more.
kolla.grade_text: {n} ads and trackers loaded without AdRaze.
kolla.grade_text_clean: Almost no ads or tracking. Nice.
kolla.consent_note: In the run without AdRaze we clicked Accept on the cookie banner, like most people do.
kolla.danger_title: This page is flagged as dangerous
kolla.danger_text: {n} of {m} security lists warn about it. We did not open it, and you should not either.
kolla.danger_cta: AdRaze stops pages like this before they open.
kolla.cta_text: AdRaze stops ads, trackers and dangerous pages. Free, forever.
kolla.how1: The link is checked against open security lists and DNS filters, including URLhaus, Phishing Army, Quad9 and Cloudflare.
kolla.how2: The page is opened in Chrome on our server, with no extensions. Every ad and tracker is counted with the same rules AdRaze uses.
kolla.how3: Then it is opened again with AdRaze installed, and we compare the two runs.
kolla.how4: Flagged pages are never opened, and the server can only reach ordinary web pages on the internet.
